# Introduction

Describe the problem pkgname solves, the kind of data it works with, and how
it relates to other Bioconductor packages. Use Bioconductor classes such as
`SummarizedExperiment` or `GRanges` for inputs and outputs where they fit.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("pkgname")
```

# Getting started

```{r setup}
library(pkgname)
```

Replace this with a worked example on real (small) data.

```{r example}
hello("Bioconductor")
sumSquaresCpp(c(1, 2, 3))    # C++ example
sumSquaresRust(c(1, 2, 3))   # Rust example
```
